historyTimeline.h2: Mazda 6 2.0-2.5 Skyactiv-G - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The third-generation Mazda 6 (GJ/GL) launched in 2012 as the first model to feature Mazda's full Skyactiv technology suite. The Skyactiv-G petrol engine family replaced the older MZR units, offering higher compression ratios (14.0:1 for the 2.0L, 13.0:1 for the 2.5L) with improved fuel economy and performance . The 2.0L was the core UK-market petrol choice, while the 2.5L became available in higher-spec trims from launch.

milestones.description: GJ generation launched with 2.0L Skyactiv-G (PE-VPS, 165hp) and 2.5L Skyactiv-G (PY-VPS, 190hp)
2014 - 2.0L and 2.5L Skyactiv-G offered across SE, SE-L, Sport and Sport Nav trims
Recall issued for 2014-2015 models with i-ELOOP system affecting PCM software
Ignition coil recall affecting 92,448 vehicles including Mazda6 with Skyactiv-G engines
GL facelift introduced; 2.0L Skyactiv-G continues with PE-VPS code, 2.5L turbo (PY-VPTS, 255hp) becomes available for higher trims
2019 - EGR valve carbon deposit misfire recall affecting Skyactiv-G 2.5L models

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Mazda 6 2.0-2.5 Skyactiv-G is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points for PE-VPS and PY-VPS units.

commonProblems.h2: Mazda 6 2.0-2.5 Skyactiv-G Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Mazda 6 2.0-2.5 Skyactiv-G petrol engines are generally regarded as reliable and fuel-efficient units. However, as direct-injection petrol engines, they have well-documented weaknesses: carbon buildup on intake valves, ignition coil failures, EGR valve carbon deposits causing misfire, and PCM software issues . Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Carbon Buildup on Intake Valves - The Direct Injection Achilles' Heel
problems.rootCause: Direct injection engines inject fuel directly into the combustion chamber, bypassing the intake valves. Over time, oil blow-by and crankcase ventilation deposits accumulate carbon on the intake valves, leading to restricted airflow, misfires, rough idle, and reduced power . Some discussions note that Mazda DI engines are less plagued by this issue than some competitors, but periodic cleaning is still recommended .

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Fuel system cleaner, new spark plugs
repairOptions.longevity: Preventative; may temporarily improve mild symptoms

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Media-blasting of intake valves to remove carbon deposits, new intake manifold gaskets
repairOptions.longevity: Effective for moderate buildup; restores performance

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, rebuilt PE-VPS/PY-VPS with serviced injectors, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If carbon buildup has caused valve or piston damage

problems.recommendation: The Skyactiv-G petrol is fundamentally robust, but preventative maintenance is essential. If your Mazda 6 2.0-2.5 Skyactiv-G is approaching 60,000+ miles and you're noticing rough idle or hesitation, consider professional intake valve cleaning (walnut blasting) before considering replacement. This is significantly cheaper than a full engine rebuild and addresses the most common failure point.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt PE-VPS Mazda 6 2.0 Skyactiv-G engine prices

problems.rootCause: In 2015, Mazda recalled 92,448 vehicles with 2.0L and 2.5L Skyactiv-G engines due to ignition coil failures . Under high-temperature conditions, the ignition coils could enter a protection mode, causing one cylinder to stop firing - resulting in engine shaking, loss of power, and the engine warning light illuminating . The recall affected 2013-2015 model year CX-5 and Mazda3 vehicles; a similar issue affected Mazda6 models .

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace all 4 ignition coils with updated units; PCM reprogramming
repairOptions.longevity: If under recall: free; if not, replace all 4 coils preventatively

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace all 4 spark plugs with correct specification

problems.recommendation: Check your Mazda 6 VIN against the 2015 ignition coil recall. The replacement was free for affected vehicles and included updated coils and PCM software . If you're experiencing misfire symptoms and your vehicle wasn't covered, replacing all four coils and spark plugs as a set is recommended.

problems.h4: EGR Valve Carbon Deposits - Misfire at Idle
problems.rootCause: Carbon deposits may be pinched at the EGR valve seat, preventing the valve from closing completely. The closed position of the EGR valve is learned improperly as it is not equipped with a position sensor. While idling, EGR gas improperly mixes with fresh air, causing misfire and DTC P0300 . PCM reprogramming resolves the issue.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Software update to force learning of EGR valve closed position when misfire detected
repairOptions.longevity: First-line fix; may be covered under warranty

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Clean or replace EGR valve, replace gasket (P/N PY8V-20-305)

problems.recommendation: If your 2018-2019 Mazda 6 2.5L Skyactiv-G experiences rough idle at start, have the PCM checked for updated software. The recall fix reprograms the PCM to force learning of the closed position of the EGR valve when a misfire is detected at idle .

problems.rootCause: The PCM may incorrectly determine that there is a failure of the system energy storage capacitor when the vehicle is operating under heavy rain or through deep puddles. The charging system may stop operating, draining the battery and eventually causing the engine to stop .

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Reprogram the PCM with modified software

problems.recommendation: Check your Mazda 6 VIN for the i-ELOOP recall. The inspection and repair will be performed free of charge, and may take approximately half an hour to complete .

finalCta.h4: Don't Let Engine Failure Write Off Your Mazda 6 2.0-2.5 Skyactiv-G
finalCta.paragraph: The Skyactiv-G petrol engine is generally robust, but direct injection carbon buildup, ignition coil issues, and EGR valve problems can cause significant issues over time . Preventative maintenance - including walnut blasting at 60,000-80,000 miles and checking for outstanding recalls - can extend your engine's life. items.question: Is the Mazda 6 2.0-2.5 Skyactiv-G a reliable engine?
items.answer: The Skyactiv-G petrol engines are generally regarded as reliable and fuel-efficient, with many owners reporting 200,000+ miles with regular maintenance. However, as direct injection engines, carbon buildup on intake valves is a well-documented issue that requires preventative maintenance . A 2015 ignition coil recall affected 92,448 vehicles with 2.0L and 2.5L Skyactiv-G engines . A 2018-2019 EGR valve carbon deposit misfire recall affected Mazda6 2.5L models . With regular maintenance and the recalls addressed, the Skyactiv-G is a durable unit.
keyPoints: Carbon buildup is the main long-term issue
2015 ignition coil recall and 2018-2019 EGR recall issued
items.cta: -> Check your Mazda 6 VIN for recalls

items.question: Does the Mazda 6 2.0-2.5 Skyactiv-G have a timing belt or chain?
items.answer: The Mazda 6 2.0-2.5 Skyactiv-G uses a timing chain, not a belt . The chain is designed for the life of the engine with proper servicing. There's no scheduled replacement interval, but regular oil changes with the correct specification are essential for timing chain longevity - lack of lubrication can cause chain stretch and tensioner issues .
keyPoints: Regular oil changes critical for chain life

items.question: What are the signs of carbon buildup on a Mazda 6 2.0-2.5 Skyactiv-G?
items.answer: Common signs of carbon buildup on intake valves include rough idle, hesitation on acceleration, reduced power, misfire codes (P0300-P0304), and poor fuel economy . The Skyactiv-G is susceptible to carbon buildup due to its direct injection design . Professional walnut blasting is the most effective solution, typically costing £400-£700 at an independent specialist.
